To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
urban screens have the potential to become an important part of the public space, and that they are a good example of the privatization of the public space.
urban screens are not just screens, they are public spaces, and that their content and the way they are used, is not neutral.
urban screens can be used to create a sense of community and belonging in the urban space and to create opportunities for dialogue and engagement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: 1) The use of screens as public spaces for the display of images and the potential for the display of other kinds of content.

1) the use of screens in Times Square to display art and its relation to the branding of the area; 2) the content of the art displayed and its potential to generate a dialogue with the public; 3) the use of urban screens in the display of art and social issues and its potential to broaden public engagement in public space; 4) the potential of urban screens to include public space as a site for dialogue and engagement.
the role and function of urban screens as public spaces and the potential for the display of cultural content that can broaden participation in the use and understanding of the city.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the urban screens in Times Square, New York City, are used as a means for the display of advertisement, but they also provide an opportunity for the display of other contents, including art and social issues, and that the use of these screens can be seen not only as token screens that are used for the branding of the City but also as a means of public participation and engagement.

the urban screen is not just a digital substitute for billboards, but a public space that has the potential to be used as a window to engage with a community, to display social issues and art, and to provide a context that can broaden the understanding of the image displayed.

the use of screens for the purpose of advertising is not the only possible use of screens, and that screens have the potential for the display of a wide range of content, that could be used for the purpose of public engagement, and the display of art, as well as social issues, that could be seen as opportunities for difference.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

urban screens are not just a technological innovation but rather a new form of urban space that can be used for different kinds of social and cultural practices that go beyond the commercialisation of public space.
urban screens are not just digital billboards but rather public spaces for social engagement and cultural exchange.

the use of screens for the display of video art in Times Square has the potential to broaden participation and engagement with the city, and to include the public as a stakeholder in the branding of cities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
screens can be a site of public engagement that can be used by artists and other cultural producers to address social issues.
the use of urban screens to display art is a new opportunity for the city to be seen as a cultural space, and for artists and the public to participate and engage in the public space.
the urban screen is a space for dialogue, a space for the inclusion of the community, a space for art and a space for the city.
